key_insight: A connectome’s apparent functional advantage can reflect how unmeasured physiology is tuned rather than the wiring itself.
engineering_relevance: For computational model comparisons, match optimisation effort and constrain nuisance parameters with independent data before attributing performance gains to structure.
method: Compare real-wiring physiology transferred to nulls (P1) with physiology tuned separately for each wiring (P2).
Restrict independent tuning to physiology consistent with external data (P3).
Test conclusions using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.
evidence_signal: In the mushroom-body model, the real-wiring advantage changed from +0.09 under P1/P2 to −0.09 under P3, with 95% confidence intervals excluding zero and confirmation in held-out runs.
watch_item: Data-constrained physiology can expose model inadequacy: failure under those constraints does not establish a deficit in biological wiring.
paper_title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
